title: Centralize line-ending normalization at entry point; document LF-precondition on helpers
context: CommonMark recognizes three line endings (CRLF, LF, lone CR). The prior fix for issue #298 only normalized CRLF pairs. More fundamentally, regex-based fence/span detection (using . and $ anchors) assumes LF-normalized text; absent normalization, CRLF checkouts miss fence boundaries and misclassify example markers as live anchors.
decision: Changed parseDocAnchors's normalization regex from /\r\n/g to /\r\n?/g to catch all three line-ending forms in one place. Added explicit LF-normalized-input preconditions to fencedRanges and inlineSpanRanges docstrings, each citing the actual mechanism that makes it sensitive to unnormalized input.
consequences: All line-ending variants now normalized uniformly at the single entry point
Precondition documentation on helpers catches future direct-call violations at review time

fencedRanges is CRLF-sensitive (its fence-line regex's . excludes \r) and inlineSpanRanges is lone-CR-sensitive (split("\n") doesn't split a bare CR, so same-line backtick pairing can span logical lines) — both real, distinct mechanisms; a lone-CR regression test fails without the /\r\n?/g widening, proving inlineSpanRanges was affected too
Mixed LF/CRLF documents, unclosed CRLF fences, and a lone-CR document pinned with new test cases
alternatives_rejected: Normalize line endings separately in each helper (fencedRanges, inlineSpanRanges, MARKER) — scattered logic, unclear contracts, easier to miss a call site
Handle lone CR only when encountered — leaves edge case exploitable and obscures the root precondition
